Team Leader Qi Zhang, Bowen Zhou B. Benchmark Evaluation Settings The configurations below describe evaluations conducted by us. Published scores retain the settings of their source evaluations; the three leading reference columns are excluded from the six-model rankings. 35 B.1. Agentic Coding Terminal-Bench 2.1 [61]. Evaluations use Claude Code on 89 tasks. Task timeouts are multiplied by 12, capped at 12 hours; verifier timeouts are multiplied by 3. The verifier uses offline dependencies. Runs allow up to 1,000 interaction steps, 512K context window, 64K output per generation and max thinking effort. Resources follow each task specification; agents can access network resources through mirrors, while image/PDF reading is disabled. Errors score zero. Each model evaluated here is run in four independent runs and the mean pass rate is reported. The GPT-6 Astra reference score is taken from the official leaderboard [62]. DeepSWE [63, 64]. Evaluations use the AgentCompass framework on DeepSWE v1.1, which contains 113 tasks. The evaluation harness is mini-swe-agent v2.4.2 with the official mini.yaml configuration. Temperature and top_p are both 1.0. Each task receives 2 CPUs and 8 GiB of memory. Agent and verifier have no external network access; there is no step or cost cap. Commands have 30-second timeout and model requests 600-second timeout. The task budget is 6 5,400 seconds, or 32,400 seconds. Hidden tests run in separate verifier sandbox with 1,800-second timeout. Pass rate is computed from binary rewards; model timeouts and context overflow count as failures. The reported pass rate is the average of four independent runs per evaluated model. NL2Repo-Bench [65]. DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017, GLM-5.3-Flash, Claude Opus 5 and Sage S2.1 Flash are run with Claude Code, and the other models with OpenHands (v0.56.0). Sage S2.1 Flash is evaluated with 512K context window. The score is the average test pass rate over 104 tasks. SWE-bench Pro [66]. For SWE-bench Pro, Sage S2.1 Flash, GLM-5.3-Flash, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash1017 and Claude Opus 5 use Claude Code, while the other evaluated models use OpenHands. The evaluation uses the official V2 locked-protocol prompt wrapper [67] and the v1 task set of 731 tasks. Each task receives 4 CPUs and 16 GiB of memory, 4.5-hour time limit and at most 250 turns. Output is capped at 64K tokens per generation and thinking effort is set to max. External network access is disabled except for model endpoints, and Git history after the base commit is removed to prevent information leakage or benchmark contamination. Image/PDF reading, WebSearch and WebFetch are disabled. Patches are collected using git diff after the agent finishes and graded with official tests in an isolated sandbox. B.2. Productivity SpreadsheetBench 2 [68]. GPT-5.6 Sol uses Codex, while the other evaluated models use Claude Code. Visualization tasks are graded by Qwen3.7-plus [69] as VLM verifier, while the remaining tasks use rule-based verifiers. The reported score is the weighted average accuracy over 321 tasks. Evaluations use the Harbor framework, with 1 CPU and 10 GB of memory allocated to each task. Each model request has 60-minute timeout, and there is no interaction-step limit. For Visualization tasks, charts are rendered on Windows before grading. ALE-CLI [70]. Evaluations use the CLI subset of Agents Last Exam v1 with Claude Code. Agents complete multi-step workflows in the prescribed software environments and submit deliverables, checked against version-matched hidden references and deterministic graders. Environments and task assets follow v1. Our configuration differs from the official evaluation setup in the following respects: we use 512K context window, set max_tokens to 96K, and allow 10 hours per task. For 36 business_finance/pe_screening_memo_1/zscaler_fy2025, grading uses gpt-6.1-sol instead of the gpt-4o-mini specified in the official configuration. APEX-Agents [71]. Evaluations use v1.1 task definitions and grading rubrics for cross-file workflows in investment banking, management consulting and corporate law. Agents produce deliverables from task materials for rubric-based evaluation. task succeeds only if all rubric criteria pass. We report pass@1, the task success rate for single attempt. Execution uses an in-house harness and retains the v1.1 grading changes for noncommittal answers. The interaction-step limit is higher than in the official configuration. GDPval [44]. Evaluations use the AgentCompass framework on 220 tasks. Sage S2.1 Flash and GLM-5.3-Flash use Claude Code; DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017, Qwen3.8-Max, GPT-5.6 Sol and Claude Opus 5 use OpenHands. Each task receives 4 CPUs and 8 GiB of memory, 4-hour agent timeout and at most 250 turns. Output is capped at 64K tokens with max thinking effort. WebSearch, WebFetch and image/PDF reading are disabled. GLM-5.2 at temperature 0 judges candidate deliverables against Claude Opus 4.8 deliverables, applying rubric criteria and recording wins, losses and ties. The reported metric is the number of wins divided by the total number of evaluations. Ties remain in the denominator but contribute no wins; no half-win credit is assigned. Workspace-Bench-Lite [43]. Evaluations use the English Lite dataset and the AgentCompass framework. GPT-5.6 Sol uses Codex, while the other evaluated models use Claude Code. Each task receives 2 CPUs and 8 GiB of memory and has two-hour time limit. The LLM judge is doubao-seed2-1-lite-260915 [72]. Workspace-Bench [43]. Evaluations use the English Full dataset. GPT-5.6 Sol uses Codex, while the other evaluated models use Claude Code. Each task receives 2 CPUs and 8 GiB of memory and has two-hour time limit. The LLM judge is doubao-seed-2-1-lite-260915. B.3. Tool Use OfficeQA Pro [59]. The 133 tasks in OfficeQA Pro are evaluated using Claude Code as the harness, with network access enabled. Each model request has 1,800-second timeout, and each task attempt has 3,600-second timeout, with up to two retries on timeout and limit of 200 steps. Answers are extracted and scored using EvalScopes OfficeQA scoring logic with zero tolerance. Tasks without valid result are counted as incorrect in the overall score across all 133 tasks. Harvey LAB [73]. Evaluations use 120-task subset sampled proportionally from the 1,200 official tasks. GLM-5.2 serves as the LLM judge. The reported score is the proportion of tasks that pass every rubric criterion. AutomationBench [74]. Evaluations use v1.0.6 with an in-house harness and include the null-type handling fix from AutomationBench PR 13. Tasks start from predefined business states and use tools to complete workflows. Official assertion-based rubrics check final states; task passes only when every assertion passes. The reported metric is task pass rate, excluding the simple domain. 37 BFCL V4 [75]. Web Search tests use Serper, and samples with API failures are scored as incorrect. Evaluations use the official harness at commit 6ea5797 on 5,217 cases, with 16 concurrent workers. Temperature is set to 0.001. Each request has 120-second timeout and allows at most 2 attempts. The overall score assigns weights of 10% to Non-Live, 10% to Live, 10% to Irrelevance, 30% to Multi-Turn and 40% to Agentic. Within Agentic, Web Search and Memory receive equal weight. JobBench [76]. Evaluations use the official OpenCode harness on the main split of 65 tasks, with 10 concurrent workers. Each task has 7,200-second timeout and allows at most 2 attempts. Grok4.3 [77] serves as the judge, and the final score is the mean of the per-task percentage scores. Tasks with API failures or two failed attempts receive score of zero. SkillsBench [78]. Evaluations use OpenHands on the 79-task subset that excludes multimodal tasks. Results are averaged over three runs. 𝜏3-bench Banking [79]. Evaluations use the 97 Banking Knowledge tasks and Tau2 commit a2c0247. Both the user simulator and the judge use GPT-5.2 [80] with low reasoning effort, and the random seed is 300. The alltools configuration provides BM25 search, dense retrieval using text-embedding3-large [81] with the top 10 results, and read-only knowledge-base shell. The knowledge base contains 698 documents. Each model request has 180-second timeout and allows up to 3 retries. Simulations have 1,800-second timeout, while the outer task timeout is 2,400 seconds. Each task allows at most 200 interaction steps. B.4. ML Engineering MLE-bench Lite [35]. Evaluations use the Lite dataset and the Claude Code harness, with 12-hour time limit per run. The reported metric is HumanRank, calculated following Frontis-MA1 [82]: the mean percentage of human leaderboard participants surpassed by the selected submission. PostTrainBench [37, 83]. Evaluations use v1.2. Scores for GLM-5.3-Flash, GPT-5.6 Sol and Claude Opus 5 are taken from the official leaderboard at posttrainbench.com, weighted average over 24 benchmarkbase-model combinations (6 benchmarks 4 base models). The score for Sage S2.1 Flash comes from our own evaluations and uses the same weighted average over the 24 benchmarkbasemodel combinations. PaperBench [36]. Evaluations cover all 20 papers of the official Code-Dev variant. GPT-5.6 Sol uses Codex and other models use Claude Code, with max thinking effort. Each task receives 4 CPUs and 16 GB of memory, no GPU, and 12-hour limit, with search and page-reading access. GLM-5.3 [84] serves as the judge and scores each rubric leaf; the final score is the mean across 20 papers. MLS-Bench [85]. Evaluations use Claude Code as the execution harness to propose and implement improvements to machine learning methods within the scope of changes permitted by each official task. Task evaluators test transfer across models, datasets and random seeds. Scores use the official normalized task metric. 38 B.5. Deep Research DeepResearch Bench II [86, 87]. Evaluations use Claude Code. All models use the same search tools, and each task has four-hour time limit. Each result is the mean of three judge scores.
